summary: Yakima County, WA site of an L-5 cab dated to the 1930s, removed or destroyed in 1960; concrete, a foundation and debris remain at the summit.

facts.design: L-5 cab (reported by the Register and firelookout.com; Willhite has found no photos of it)
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1960 (sources differ on the word); concrete, a foundation and debris remain at the summit per Willhite's photos, including 2016 views

access.note: Reached over FR 1706 from Highway 410 and then a short old blocked road; Willhite says the road is rough and needs high clearance; no closure is described

visit.trail_note: From the last parking area, an old blocked road climbs a steep hillside, about five minutes and 150 feet of gain (Willhite)

events.note: Decade only: the Register and firelookout.com say 1930s. Willhite argues the cab came after the July 1936 panoramas
Panorama photos taken July 31, 1936 show no structure or improvements at the site (Willhite)
Register says removed in 1960; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1960
Registered July 19, 2012 as US 1359, WA 259; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the cab was removed in 1960; firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1960. The story reports both and does not choose.

resolved_conflicts.field: existence and date of the cab
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com describe a 1930s L-5 cab. Willhite says other sources describe only a tent and fire finder, and that the 1936 panoramas show no structure, so any cab came later. He still believes a cab existed.

notes_for_editor: No staffing or fire records found; one search returned nothing site-specific, so none are included. The 1930 built-event year is a decade placeholder (sources say 1930s). Willhite's photos, including 2016 views, are the only view of the site today. Brief's 'ground' kind fits the concrete foundation but no source states it. Forest name is the Register's and was not checked against a current Forest Service source.
